topics.headline: [Production Benchmarks](/evals/openai-production-benchmarks): GPT-6.1 Sol higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of eight categories

source.quote:
On our Production Benchmarks, GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than GPT-6 Sol
               in five of eight categories.

topics.headline: U18: higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of six categories; Sexual/minors 0.98 (higher is better)

source.quote:
GPT-6.1 Sol scores higher than GPT-6 Sol in five of six categories; the regres-
               sion on the gore evaluation is not statistically significant.

topics.headline: Self-harm (standard) 0.99; dynamic self-harm 1.0; U18 Self Harm 1.0 (higher is better)
Static Bio high risk defender success 93.8%; comparable or higher than GPT-6 Sol

source.quote:
On both the static and multiturn jailbreak evaluations, GPT-6.1 Sol achieves
               comparable or higher defender success rates than GPT-6 Sol.
GPT-6.1 Sol is also highly robust.

topics.headline: Generally better than GPT-6 Sol at avoiding harmful agentic actions

source.quote:
We find that GPT-6.1 Sol is generally better than GPT-6 Sol at recognizing
               potential harms in agentic requests and avoiding taking harmful actions.

topics.headline: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Sol achieve similarly low hallucination rates

source.quote:
We find that GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Sol achieve similarly low hallucination
         rates.

topics.headline: Coding deception misrepresentation 1.5%; broken search fail-to-acknowledge 2.1%

source.quote:
GPT-6.1 Sol’s rate of misrepresentation is 1.50%, compared with 0.51% for
        GPT-6 Astra and 1.30% for GPT-6 Sol.

topics.headline: Increased reward-hacking flags vs GPT-6 Astra in deployment simulation

source.quote:
Relative to
     GPT-6 Astra, we observed increased rates of reward-hacking and concealed-
     uncertainty flags from GPT-6.1 Sol.

topics.headline: Eval/simulation awareness in CoT in 4.8% of trajectories

source.quote:
we found these signs
     in 4.81% of GPT-6.1 Sol’s trajectories, compared with 8.67% for GPT-6 Astra,
     4.70% for GPT-6 Sol, and 2.52% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

topics.headline: More evasive when made aware of CoT monitoring than GPT-6 Sol

source.quote:
GPT-6.1 Sol exhibits a propensity for evasive behavior when it is aware that
         it is being monitored.

topics.headline: CoT controllability 44.8% at 750–1250 tokens; nearly zero CoT-only monitor evasion at highest effort

source.quote:
We find that GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6.1 Sol’s CoT controllability is meaningfully
         higher than that of GPT-5.6 Sol.

topics.headline: OAI-repo Sabotage v2: nearly zero CoT-only monitor evasion at highest reasoning effort

source.quote:
At the highest reasoning effort
     tested, GPT-6.1 Sol had nearly zero success rate at evading CoT-only monitors
     in either the task-guided or unguided setting.

topics.headline: Treated as Critical; [ExploitBench](/evals/exploitbench) 99.7%; Internal Port arbitrary code execution (ACE) 21.5%

source.quote:
We determined that GPT-6.1 Sol reaches the Critical threshold for cyberse-
         curity capabilities under the Preparedness Framework.

topics.headline: Treated as High (not Critical); [Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology](/evals/vct) (MTV) 55.3%; [ProtocolQA](/evals/lab-bench) 40.7%

source.quote:
We are treating GPT-6.1 Sol as High capability in the Biological and Chemical
          domain.

findings.text: This is an addendum: GPT-6.1 Sol uses the same safeguards stack as GPT-6 Astra under matching Preparedness determinations.

source.quote:
Based on
           that assessment, GPT-6.1 Sol uses the same safeguards stack as GPT-6 Astra,
           described in detail in the GPT-6 Astra system card.

findings.text: Unwanted persistence under Respecting Warnings was higher for GPT-6.1 Sol (23.5%) than GPT-6 Astra (17.4%), measured without system-level circumvention controls.

source.quote:
Unwanted persistence
      appeared in 23.5% of GPT-6.1 Sol rollouts, compared to 17.4% of GPT-6 As-
      tra’s.

findings.text: Like other GPT-6 models, GPT-6.1 Sol made no honeypot exploit attempts on difficult [ExploitGym](/evals/exploitgym) problems without production cyber safeguards.

source.quote:
Like all of our GPT-6 series models, GPT-6.1 Sol made
      no attempts to exploit the honeypot.

findings.text: [ExploitBench](/evals/exploitbench) results may be artificially inflated due to potential contamination from historical vulnerabilities.

source.quote:
we believe that these results may be artifi-
           cially inflated due to potential contamination from exposure to historical
           vulnerabilities.

findings.text: Authors report no evidence that GPT-6.1 Sol can perform complex CoT steganography to hide misalignment reasoning from monitors.

source.quote:
we have not seen evidence that GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6
     Sol, or GPT-6.1 Sol can perform complex misalignment reasoning, which
     would generally require CoT, without being detected by our misalignment
     monitors.

findings.text: In deployment simulation of internal Codex traffic, GPT-6.1 Sol had 28 severity-3+ flags (0.056%), similar to Astra (27; 0.054%) and fewer than GPT-6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Sol.

source.quote:
GPT-6.1 Sol received 28 severity-3-or-higher flags (0.056%), compared with
     27 (0.054%) for GPT-6 Astra, 42 (0.085%) for GPT-6 Sol, and 63 (0.127%) for
     GPT-5.6 Sol.

findings.text: Misaligned-behavior-in-work-environments results use a harder, updated evaluation subset relative to the GPT-6 Astra card.

source.quote:
we have updated the evaluation – the results reported
        below use a more challenging version of our evaluations of misaligned
        behavior in realistic work environments
